note: Attacker-controlled serviceData from the CLI is measured and truncated to 8 bits, so the raw input length becomes the service-data length field.
The attacker-controlled serviceData bytes are copied into the service config buffer and later forwarded into the network-data API.
Attacker-controlled serverData is likewise measured and truncated to 8 bits, creating the server-data length used downstream.
The attacker-controlled serverData bytes are copied into the config buffer and passed to the service-add API.
The CLI-provided lengths and buffers are propagated unchanged into Local::AddService, preserving attacker control over both payload sizes.
The total TLV size is computed in an 8-bit variable, so large attacker-controlled lengths can wrap and understate the required allocation size.
The wrapped length is used to reserve too little space for the new Service TLV, setting up an out-of-bounds write when the payload is copied.
The attacker-controlled serviceData is written into the TLV body using the untrusted length, extending beyond the under-allocated region when the size wrapped.
The attacker-controlled serverData is copied immediately after the server header; with the earlier size wrap, this memcpy can overrun the network-data buffer and crash the target.
